To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prostaglandins are mediators of the phorbol esters in vivo, and that prostaglandines are involved in the induction of mouse skin tumor promotion.

prostaglandins are required for the mitogenic effect in mouse skin of the tumor promoter phorbolester, TPA, and that this requirement is restricted to the initial phase of cell proliferation, the first hour.

prostaglandins E2 and F2α are potent mitogens for mouse epidermal basal cells and that the mitogenic effect is mediated by cyclic AMP and is inhibited by prostaglandins F2α and A2 and by dibutyryl cAMP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of arachidonic acid metabolites in the regulation of cell proliferation in mouse epidermal cells in vivo.
the mechanism of action of the phorbolesters, and in particular with the mechanism whereby these compounds induce hyperproliferation in mouse epidermal cells in vivo.
the mechanism by which the phorbolesters induce hyperplasia in the mouse skin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
indomethacin inhibits cell proliferation in mouse epidermal cells induced by the phorbol esters TPA or 4-0-methyl TPA in vivo.
the mitogenic effect in the skin of TPA, a tumor promoter, is mediated by prostaglandins.
the mitogenic effect is mediated via the prostaglandin pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prostaglandins are important for the control of epidermal cell proliferation and that this control may be mediated via the arachidonic acid cascade.
indomethacin inhibits the mitogenic effect but not the inflammatory response of TPA in skin in vivo.
indomethacin inhibition is reversed by prostglandin E2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indomethacin inhibits the proliferative response of the epidermis to TPA by blocking the synthesis of prostaglandins.
the inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis is a useful tool in studying the role of prostaglandins in biological processes.
the inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis by indomethacin does not inhibit the inflammatory response, which is a very important finding.
